'''Izabella Mônica Vieira Teixeira''' (born 9 October 1961) was the [[Brazil]]ian [[List of Ministers of Natural Environment of Brazil|Minister of the Environment]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.un.org/sg/management/bios/Teixeira.shtml|title=Izabella Teixeira (Brazil)|publisher=[[United Nations]]|accessdate=16 January 2016}}</ref> She is the recipient of the Lifetime Achievement Award ([[Champions of the Earth]]) in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=Costa Rica named 'UN Champion of the Earth' for pioneering role in fighting climate change |url=https://www.unep.org/championsofearth/news-and-stories/costa-rica-named-un-champion-earth-pioneering-role-fighting-climate-change |website=Champions of the Earth |language=en |date=20 September 2019}}</ref>

==Education==
She was born in [[Brasília]], and has a master's degree in energy planning and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[environmental planning]] from COPPE/UFRJ ([[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro]]).<ref name=united>{{cite web|title=Izabella Teixeira|url=https://www.un.org/wcm/content/site/climatechange/pages/gsp/group-members_1/Izabella_Teixeira|website=UN Secretary-General’s High-level Panel on Global Sustainability (GSP) |accessdate=16 January 2016}}</ref>

==Early career==

In May 2010 she was appointed Minister of the Environment, and, in January 2011 she was reappointed to the position by [[Dilma Rousseff]], Brazil's new President.<ref name=united/><ref>{{cite news|author=Ana Nicolaci da Costa|url=http://www.trust.org/alertnet/news/brazil-incoming-govt-confirms-another-3-ministers|title=Brazil incoming govt confirms another 3 ministers|work=Thomson Reuters Foundation|date=16 December 2010|accessdate=11 July 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101225073743/http://www.trust.org/alertnet/news/brazil-incoming-govt-confirms-another-3-ministers/|archivedate=25 December 2010}}</ref>

== Minister of the Environment==

In October 2010 Teixeira made a statement on behalf of Brazil at the 10th conference on the [[Convention on Biological Diversity]] in [[Nagoya]], [[Japan]], in which she outlined Brazil's view that the time for talking had stopped and that compromise may be required among the various nations in order to achieve actions.<ref>{{cite news|author=Zachary Shahan |title=Brazil's Minister of the Environment: "The time for talking is over. It is time for providing answers, solutions, actions." |url=http://ecolocalizer.com/2010/10/28/brazils-minister-of-the-environment-the-time-for-talking-is-over-it-is-time-for-providing-answers-solutions-actions |newspaper=EcoLocalizer |date=28 October 2010 |accessdate=2014-03-26 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305163610/http://ecolocalizer.com/2010/10/28/brazils-minister-of-the-environment-the-time-for-talking-is-over-it-is-time-for-providing-answers-solutions-actions/ |archivedate= 5 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She also spoke at the [[2010 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] in [[Cancún]], [[Mexico]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Brazil Says UN's Proposal on Kyoto Accord Text Sends Is Best You Get|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2010-12-10/brazil-says-un-s-proposal-on-kyoto-accord-text-sends-is-best-you-get-.html|newspaper=Bloomberg |author=Jim Efstathiou Jr.|date=10 December 2010}}</ref>

At home in Brazil, she successfully hosted the Rio+20 ([[UN Conference on Sustainable Development]]) and the 2012 [[World Environment Day]].<ref name=unep>{{cite web|title=2013 Laureate – Policy Leadership (co-winner) Izabella Teixeira|url=http://www.unep.org/champions/laureates/2013/Teixeira.asp|website=United Nations Environment Programme|accessdate=11 July 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714202003/http://www.unep.org/champions/laureates/2013/Teixeira.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 24 September 2012, Teixeira was appointed by [[UN Secretary-General]] [[Ban Ki-moon]] to serve on the High-Level Panel of Eminent Persons on the [[Post-2015 Development Agenda]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Secretary-General Appoints Izabella Teixeira of Brazil to His High-Level Panel of Eminent Persons on Post-2015 Development Agenda | url = https://www.un.org/News/Press/docs/2012/sga1374.doc.htm |author=UN Press Release |date=24 September 2012}}</ref>

==Issues==

===Deforestation===
{{main|Deforestation in Brazil}}
Teixeira is devoted to reversing the [[deforestation of the Amazon Rainforest]], and achieved an 84% reduction in [[deforestation]] from 2004 to 2012, a "remarkable feat that is a tribute to her courage to push against the tide of destruction and is a significant initiative from Brazil on [[climate change mitigation]]". Her land-use planning policies saved 250,000&nbsp;km<sup>2</sup> of conservation areas—the equivalent of 75 percent of protected forests in the world.<ref name=unep/>

From August 2012 to July 2013, the rate of deforestation increased by 29% in the [[Amazônia Legal]] (Legal Amazon),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wwf.org.br/natureza_brasileira/reducao_de_impactos2/amazonia/?41242/Desmatamento-na-Amaznia-cresceu-29-entre-2012-2013|title=Desmatamento na Amazônia cresceu 29% entre 2012-2013}}</ref> and from 2013 to 2014, it rose by 358%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oglobo.globo.com/sociedade/desmatamento-na-amazonia-sobe-358-em-apenas-1-ano-13321964|title = Desmatamento na Amazônia sobe 358% em apenas 1 ano|date = 21 July 2014}}</ref> With Teixeira as Environment Minister, Brazil has also refused to sign the anti-deforestation pledge that aims to reduce deforestation by 2030, dealing a blow to the Climate Change summit that took place in New York in October 2014. “Unfortunately, we were not consulted,” Brazil’s Environment Minister Izabella Teixeira told the Associated Press.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/climate-change-summit-brazil-refuses-to-sign-un-pledge-to-slow-deforestation-9751770.html|title = Climate Change summit: Brazil refuses to sign UN's pledge to slow|date = 24 September 2014}}</ref>

===2014 FIFA World Cup===
On 24 May 2014, Teixeira announced a pollution-reducing initiative aimed at making the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] the most environmentally friendly ever by allowing companies to buy [[carbon credit]]s in [[Emissions trading|exchange]] for the right to advertise themselves as official “green seal” World Cup sponsors. In addition, along with the [[United Nations Environment Program]], Teixeira launched a project called “green passport” that promoted [[sustainable tourism]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Brazil Scores a Green Goal for the Football World Cup|url=http://greenactionnews.net/blog/brazil-scores-a-green-goal-for-the-football-world-cup/ |newspaper=Green Action News |date=2 June 2014}}</ref>
